cards.title: Uncertainty vs. Variability in Human Prediction
cards.claim: Prediction uncertainty (limited knowledge of the system) is distinct from population variability (biological variation). Uncertainty decreases with information accumulation; variability does not. Human dose prediction models must distinguish scaling methodology uncertainty from target population variability. PD uncertainty varies by biological system and is harder to generalize than PK uncertainty.
conditions: Apply to all prospective human PK/PD scenarios.
Distinguish between model structure uncertainty and parameter uncertainty.
Do not treat generic published human methodological examples as observations for the target drug.
required_inputs: Parameter estimates with associated uncertainty metrics.
Definition of the target population for variability assessment.
limitations: Tables are limited to showing uncertainty in two parameters at discrete points.
Sensitivity plots communicate uncertainty in only one parameter at a time.
Species differences in underlying biology are a major source of PD uncertainty.
cards.downstream_use: Frames the interpretation of human simulation outputs and feasibility constraints.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
